answers.falsifier: Done when (1) with HKCU Path lacking bin, install() leaves bin on the Path exactly once; (2) a second run adds nothing; (3) every existing Path entry stays byte-identical and in the same order; (4) a dry run writes nothing and reports the step; (5) off Windows the step is not_applicable and writes nothing.
answers.from_idea: none, because the red is measured on disk beside its false green: bin/proofs/test_cairn_resolves_from_powershell.py
answers.how: A new ensure_bin_on_path(*, dry_run, repo=None, env_reader=None, env_writer=None) beside ensure_journal_merge_driver in installer.py, called from install() and listed in the dry run. It reads HKCU\Environment Path with winreg, compares case-insensitively after os.path.normcase and stripping the trailing separator, and if bin is absent writes existing.rstrip(';') + ';' + bin as REG_EXPAND_SZ, then broadcasts WM_SETTINGCHANGE 'Environment' with SendMessageTimeoutW. Never setx. Off Windows it returns not_applicable. The proof injects the reader and writer, so the real registry is never touched.
answers.traces_to: Outline 5.4.3.7 (repo-root bin is the one thing on PATH); Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics).
answers.what: On Windows, `cairn install` makes sure <repo>/bin is on the persisted user Path, without duplicating it or disturbing existing entries, so `cairn` resolves in any new PowerShell with no hand step.
